pr_title: Add option to create headless windows
pr_body:
This adds the ability to pass `None` to a `Window`'s `raw_window_handle` field.
Includes a test to demonstrate how this allows for headless testing of UI related stuff which requires windows. In this case: the positioning of a button.

Closes #3754

issue_context.title: The ability to create fake windows
issue_context.body:
## What problem does this solve or what need does it fill?

When writing unit tests for the UI, access to the window is required. But since the tests run in parallel by default, it's impossible to create a real window outside of the main thread. For details, see #1720. 

## What solution would you like?

But for unit testing, a real window is not needed, it is enough to create a fake one. Currently users can add windows manually using [add](https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/blob/514754d6503b2416e5266a24b39c884ab5d90d2f/crates/bevy_window/src/windows.rs#L10) on `Windows` resource and pass a `Window` struct to it. But to create a `Window` I need to provide [RawWindowHandle](https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/blob/514754d6503b2416e5266a24b39c884ab5d90d2f/crates/bevy_window/src/window.rs#L212). I would suggest to turn this field into `Option`. This way users will be able to create dummy windows and UI plugins will know necessary stuff, like window size and scale. Currently UI plugins such as Egui work in headless mode, but crashes on any access to context because there is no associated window.
comments:
> #3439 implemented a headless mode.

Unfortunately no. I only made it work without renderer in that PR. But there is no "headless window" for now.

I am looking at implementing this, and was wondering: in bevy_render, the `RenderPlugin` requires a window handle to get a valid drawing surface.
https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/blob/44d09dc46db356d22f3f232d16398c36db4e3d10/crates/bevy_render/src/lib.rs#L127

When a window doesn't have a handle, we need to skip at least the bits of the RenderPlugin that rely on the handle for information. However, it could mean that resources and such are missing that other components rely on.
We could even forgo adding RenderPlugin in the first place, but that probably breaks even more stuff.

What is your opinion on this? I'm at this point not all to familiar with the rendering side of things to know how much I can "cut out" when there is no window without strange behavior occurring.

> What is your opinion on this?

I think it should work with `RenderPlugin`. We just need to skip everything that relies on this handle.

It turned out I didn't even need to skip any of the RenderPlugin code, as the `Surface` was already used there as an `Option`.

I can now run an app in a test with almost all of the `DefaultPlugins` added. The only one that messes things up is the `WinitPlugin` which doesn't want to be started in a separate thread.

Being able to do `.add_plugins(DefaultPlugins)`, in a test would be quite nice. As the alternative is to add each plugin (except for the WinitPlugin) separately, and that just makes it a long list :P.

Is there a way to skip the WinitPlugin (without setting the feature flag)? Or would it be better to add an option to the plugin to allow running in a separate thread?

> Is there a way to skip the WinitPlugin (without setting the feature flag)?

You can use something like `.add_plugins_with(DefaultPlugins, |group| { group.disable::<bevy::winit::WinitPlugin>() });`

> Or would it be better to add an option to the plugin to allow running in a separate thread?

On some platforms the OS requires that the event loop runs on the main thread.

> It turned out I didn't even need to skip any of the RenderPlugin code, as the Surface was already used there as an Option.

Awesome!

> Is there a way to skip the WinitPlugin (without setting the feature flag)?

Sure can: https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/blob/44d09dc46db356d22f3f232d16398c36db4e3d10/examples/app/without_winit.rs#L6
Running `DefaultPlugins` as is (e.g. with `WinitPlugin`) doesn't make sense, you don't want to create actual window in each test.

P.S.: for unit tests I would recommend to setup minimal set of plugins for each module ([here](https://github.com/gardum-game/gardum/blob/088493837227dfa7c59dfcc29cfe39d633346727/src/characters/cooldown.rs#L88) is how I set things up, for example).
For tests that require `RenderPlugin` (to run systems that use `Mesh` or `StandardMaterial`, for example), I created a custom [HeadlessPlugin](https://github.com/gardum-game/gardum/blob/088493837227dfa7c59dfcc29cfe39d633346727/src/test_utils.rs#L33) that adds `RenderPlugin` and other minimal necessary plugins and disables GPU.
With the ability to fake windows, we will be able to test UI in similar way. So looking forward to your work.

review_comments: Good point. As far as I can tell, it has never had a safety comment. I am also not experienced enough with the codebase to know why this unsafe is OK here (or maybe it even isn't, and we haven't noticed yet).
Alright. @cart / @superdump if you can quickly explain why this is safe during review that would be appreciated, but it shouldn't block this PR.

from https://docs.rs/wgpu/latest/wgpu/struct.Instance.html#safety-2:
> Raw Window Handle must be a valid object to create a surface upon and must remain valid for the lifetime of the returned surface.

These safety requirements have always been slightly spooky. That is, imo a reasonable safety comment here is `¯\_(ツ)_/¯` :).

To my knowledge, it's safe, but it's very difficult to prove that. I don't think `winit` documents that this requirement is met, so any use of this is mostly best effort.
This should return a `Result`, not an `Option` IMO.

I can see why that would make sense. Then the caller would know _why_ they didn't get a surface (no window resource for example). On the other hand, we don't actually use the reason for not getting a surface anywhere (yet?).
If this returned an error, currently we'd have to convert it back into an Option to pass it into `RequestAdapterOptions`
Hmm, that's fair. Since this isn't `pub` that's probably fine for now.
